{{short description|Professor of developmental epigenetics}}
'''Petra Hajkova''' (born 1973) {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FMedSci}} is a Professor of Developmental Epigenetics at the [[Imperial College London]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=People - Imperial College London |url=https://profiles.imperial.ac.uk/petra.hajkova |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=profiles.imperial.ac.uk}}</ref> She is also the Deputy Director of the [[MRC London Institute of Medical Sciences|MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences]], where her research group Reprogramming and Chromatin is also hosted.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Reprogramming and Chromatin Research Group {{!}} Petra Hajkova |url=https://lms.mrc.ac.uk/research-group/reprogramming-and-chromatin/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |publisher=LMS Laboratory of Medical Sciences}}</ref>

== Education ==
Petra Hajkova completed her Masters at the [[Charles University]] in Prague, and obtained her PhD at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics]] in Berlin.<ref name=":1" />

== Academic career ==
After the completion of her PhD, Petra Hajkova worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Gurdon Institute]] in Cambridge. Since 2009, she leads her own research group at the [[MRC London Institute of Medical Sciences|MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences]] in London, working on epigenetics and reprogramming.<ref name=":1" />

Hajkova is an elected [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] member since 2018,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stevens-Smith |first=Jenna |date=2018-05-14 |title=MRC LMS's Petra Hajkova elected as a member of EMBO |url=https://lms.mrc.ac.uk/petra-hajkova-elected-as-embo-member/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |publisher=LMS Laboratory of Medical Sciences}}</ref> a Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences since 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Petra Hajkova |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Petra-Hajkova-0033z000030vDZ1AAM |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=acmedsci.ac.uk}}</ref> and a member of the Board of Trustees of [[Babraham Institute]] since 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Petra Hajkova FMedSci |url=https://www.babraham.ac.uk/people/member/1136 |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=babraham.ac.uk}}</ref> She has been a member of several editorial boards of academic journals, including [[Stem Cell Reviews and Reports|Stem Cells Reviews and Reports]] and [[PLOS Biology]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Hajkova's research group is working on [[Epigenetics|epigenetic]] memory and [[reprogramming]] during mouse development. They have published seminal work on the molecular mechanisms that underlie the maintenance of epigenetic information using ''[[in vivo]]'' models.<ref name=":2" />

== Awards and distinctions ==
* 2024: Cheryll Tickle Medal from the [[British Society for Developmental Biology]].
* 2017: Mary Lyon Medal<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Mary Lyon Medal 2017 |url=https://genetics.org.uk/medals-and-prizes/winners-of-the-2017-genetics-society-medals/mary-lyon-medal-2017-2/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |publisher=Genetics Society}}</ref>
* 2015: ERC consolidator Grant<ref name=":0" />
* 2013: EMBO Young Investigator<ref name=":0" />
